blocks.task_summary: For a=3, find the two values of b such that y=x³+3x²+b has exactly two x-axis intercepts.
method_path: Vary b systematically with a=3, consider b=0 case
Find stationary points: dy/dx=3x²+6x=3x(x+2) → x=0, x=−2
Evaluate y at stationary points: y(0)=b, y(−2)=b+4
Exactly two x-intercepts when one stationary point lies on x-axis: b=0 or b+4=0 → b=0, b=−4
accepted_alternatives: Use GDC to vary b and observe intercept behaviour graphically

evidence.basis: varies the value of b with a=3 (M1); b=−4,0 (A1)

blocks.task_summary: For a=3, state the set of b values giving exactly one x-axis intercept.
method_path: One intercept when both stationary points lie on the same side of the x-axis: b<−4 or b>0

blocks.task_summary: For a=3, state the set of b values giving exactly three x-axis intercepts.
method_path: Three intercepts when stationary points lie on opposite sides of the x-axis: −4<b<0

blocks.task_summary: For a=−3, state the set of b values giving exactly two x-axis intercepts.
method_path: For a=−3: dy/dx=3x²−6x=3x(x−2) → stationary at x=0 (y=b) and x=2 (y=b−4)
Exactly two intercepts when one stationary point on x-axis: b=0 or b=4

blocks.task_summary: For a=−3, state the set of b values giving exactly one x-axis intercept.
method_path: b<0 or b>4

blocks.task_summary: For a=−3, state the set of b values giving exactly three x-axis intercepts.
For exactly three x-axis intercepts, state whether each point of zero gradient is above or below the x-axis.
method_path: With three x-intercepts, the two stationary points must lie on opposite sides of the x-axis: one above, one below

evidence.basis: one point of zero gradient is located on either side (of the x axis) (A1)

blocks.task_summary: Show that y=x³+ax²+b has points of zero gradient at P(0,b) and Q(−2a/3, 4a³/27+b).
method_path: Differentiate: dy/dx=3x²+2ax
Solve dy/dx=0: x(3x+2a)=0 → x=0 or x=−2a/3
At x=0: y=b → P(0,b) verified
Substitute x=−2a/3 into y=x³+ax²+b
Simplify: y=(−2a/3)³+a(−2a/3)²+b = −8a³/27+4a³/9+b = 4a³/27+b → Q(−2a/3, 4a³/27+b) verified
accepted_alternatives: Method 2: substitute x=0 and x=−2a/3 into dy/dx to verify zero gradient directly, then find y-coordinate of Q by substitution

evidence.basis: dy/dx=3x²+2ax (A1); attempts to solve dy/dx=0 for x (M1); x=−2a/3, 0 (A1); P(0,b) AG; substitutes expression for x into y=x³+ax²+b (M1); simplifies to 4a³/27+b (A1); Q AG

blocks.task_summary: For a>0, b>0, find d²y/dx² and determine whether P and Q are local maximum or minimum.
method_path: d²y/dx²=6x+2a
At P(0,b): d²y/dx²=2a>0 (since a>0) → P is a local minimum
At Q(−2a/3, 4a³/27+b): d²y/dx²=6(−2a/3)+2a=−2a<0 → Q is a local maximum

evidence.basis: d²y/dx²=6x+2a (A1); at x=0, d²y/dx²=2a (>0) so P is local minimum (R1); at x=−2a/3, d²y/dx²=−2a so Q is local maximum (R1)

blocks.task_summary: For a>0, b>0, determine whether P and Q are above or below the x-axis.
method_path: b>0 → y-coordinate of P is positive → P above x-axis
a>0 and b>0 → 4a³/27+b>0 → y-coordinate of Q positive → Q above x-axis
Both points are above the x-axis
accepted_alternatives: Accept a labelled sketch clearly showing both points above the x-axis

evidence.basis: (P and Q are) both above (the x axis) (A1)

blocks.task_summary: For a<0, b>0, state whether P is a local maximum or minimum and whether above or below the x-axis.
method_path: With a<0: d²y/dx² at P = 2a < 0 → P is a local maximum
b>0 → P is above the x-axis

evidence.basis: (P) is a (local) maximum (point) and is above (the x axis) (A1)

blocks.task_summary: For a<0, b>0, state the conditions on a and b for Q to be below the x-axis.
method_path: Q below x-axis when its y-coordinate is negative: 4a³/27+b<0
accepted_alternatives: Accept equivalent forms such as b<−4a³/27 or a labelled sketch

evidence.basis: (Q is below the x axis when) 4a³/27+b<0 (A1)

blocks.task_summary: Prove that if 4a³b+27b²<0 then y=x³+ax²+b has exactly three x-axis intercepts.
method_path: Factorize: 4a³b+27b²<0 → b(4a³+27b)<0 → b(4a³/27+b)<0
Product negative → b and (4a³/27+b) have opposite signs
b is y-coordinate of P; 4a³/27+b is y-coordinate of Q
P and Q lie on opposite sides of the x-axis
For a cubic, stationary points on opposite sides of x-axis ⟺ exactly three x-intercepts
Therefore the condition implies exactly three x-intercepts
accepted_alternatives: Method 2: case analysis — b>0 and 4a³/27+b<0 ⇒ a<0 ⇒ three intercepts; or b<0 and 4a³/27+b>0 ⇒ a>0 ⇒ three intercepts

evidence.basis: attempts to factorize 4a³b+27b²<0 (M1); b(4a³+27b)<0 (A1); both cases b>0 and 4a³/27+b<0 or b<0 and 4a³/27+b>0 (A1); opposite sign → P and Q on either side (R1); on either side iff exactly three x-intercepts (R1); AG
